question: Venture-backed founders whose first company failed started another. Compared with first-time founders, how likely was the new one to succeed?
answer: About the same. Gompers and colleagues found first-time founders succeeded about 22% of the time and founders with an earlier success about 30%, while founders who had failed did no better than first-timers. Failure carried no measurable edge; success did.
move: Learning from failure is a claim to test, not a given.
ask: What have I actually learned from my last failure, and could I show it in my next attempt?
trap: Assuming what a failure teaches must show in the next attempt.
source: Gompers and colleagues, Journal of Financial Economics, 2010
reference: Gompers, Kovner, Lerner and Scharfstein, Performance persistence in entrepreneurship, Journal of Financial Economics, 2010
